Every claim the diff makes, judged against the tree and by running it:

1. The one reader. `contractReviewHeadMatch(body, headSha)` no longer scans the body: it calls `contractReviewHeadSha(body)`, which walks the comment line by line and returns the capture of the FIRST line matching `CONTRACT_REVIEW_HEAD_SHA_LINE`, and then answers that sha only when it is a case-insensitive prefix of `headSha`. The key half of the new regex is byte-for-byte `keyLineRegex('Head-sha')`'s key half (blockquote, bullet, bold and backticks around the key, then the colon); the value half is `(?:[ \t]|\*\*)*` followed by `H51_SHA_SPAN.source`, so the span must be the first thing after the colon and must be hex of 7 to 40 characters inside its own backticks. The regex is built from `.source`, so the module-level `g` flag of `H51_SHA_SPAN` is not inherited and no `lastIndex` leaks between calls. TRUE as described in the PR body and the docblock.
2. The erratum (comment 6518406382). The PR body's identifier `CONTRACT_REVIEW_40b5a25e2613a303370e9af09a030b2f982a8961_LINE` is a body-builder slip; the code at check-half-states.mjs:12629 exports `CONTRACT_REVIEW_HEAD_SHA_LINE` and nothing in the tree carries the sha-substituted name (grep over the worktree: zero hits). VERIFIED.
3. One shared definition, no drift. Consumers of the head reading at the head, by grep over the whole tree: `latestContractReviewOnHead` (check-half-states, used by `h43HandoffReading` :10257 and the H51 battery), `locateReviewOfRecord` (record-recognisers :2012 and :2039), `recordReading` in check-owed-reviews (:204, through `locateReviewOfRecord`), the queue guard's `recordVerdict` (:979, through the lazily loaded `locate`, which `loadRecordRecognisers` binds to `locateReviewOfRecord`). post-stamped.mjs imports only `CONTRACT_REVIEW_HEADING_MARKER`. No other file imports `H51_SHA_SPAN`, `contractReviewHeadMatch` or `contractReviewHeadSha`; the other `{7,40}` regexes under scripts/pm and ui/scripts are the hand-off, hold, claim and Regen-provenance key-line readers (`shaMeets`, their own lines), queue-ref parsers and CLI argument validation, none a record head reader. ui/scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs has no record reading of its own. objectui and hotcrm checkouts carry no script reading `## Contract review` or `Head-sha` (the single objectui grep hit is a prose comment in a types test). The four scripts agree through one definition. TRUE.
4. The sibling line readers. `contractReviewHandoff` (:909), `contractReviewClaims` (:1203 via `shaMeets`) and `contractReviewHold` each read the head off their own key line's tail regex (`HANDOFF_TAIL` :849, `HOLD_HEAD` :1122, `HEAD_REF` :1262) and never through `contractReviewHeadMatch`; the diff leaves them untouched, which is right.
5. The core question, answered by execution. A probe (scratchpad `probe.mjs`) imported the four modules from a worktree at the PR head and from a worktree at `origin/main`, built 23 synthetic record bodies and the live PR #27964 thread (10 comments fetched by REST, saved as a fixture), and drove each through `contractReviewHeadMatch`, `latestContractReviewOnHead`, `locateReviewOfRecord`, `recordReading` and the guard's `recordVerdict` (recognisers from `loadRecordRecognisers()`, a `.claude/**` Tier S path, repo `objectstack`), at head B (`b3d92fee…`) and head A (`8216bec4…`). Results at the PR head:
   - delta record on A whose prose names B (two 8-hex spans and one full 40-hex span): at B every reader answers null / null / absent / stale / absent; at A every reader answers A / A / found / current / stands.
   - the same with `Head-sha: ` and B's span written MID-sentence (not line-initial): B absent, A found.
   - a second line-initial `Head-sha:` B line, or a blockquoted one, BELOW the record's own line: B absent, A found (first line wins).
   - the old heading dialect naming B in the `## Contract review` heading with a `Head-sha:` A line: B absent, A found.
   - the three retired dialects (head in the heading in the TIER spelling, `Head:` on the first body line, the adoption sentence), a prose-only sha, the key folded into the span, a bare hex value, a lowercase key, a 6-hex span, an italic-wrapped span, a non-breaking space after the colon and a 41-hex span: absent at both heads.
   - a 7-hex abbreviation of B, CRLF line endings, no space before the span and trailing prose on the line: found at B, absent at A.
   - live PR #27964 thread truncated before 06:15Z (records 6515936468 on `7237921e` and 6516042954 on `8216bec4` only), at the PR's real head B: null / null / absent / stale / absent; at A: found 6516042954 / current / stands. The full thread, with record 6516322954 on B present: found 6516322954 at B. The same truncated thread through the `origin/main` readers: `contractReviewHeadMatch` answers `b3d92fee` on four comments including record 6516042954, `locateReviewOfRecord` found 6516042954, `recordReading` current, `recordVerdict` stands. The measured defect reproduces on base and is closed on the head, at all three consumers, exactly as the PR body states.
   So after this PR no guard accepts a PASS for a head named only in prose, in the heading, on a retired first-body line or in an adoption sentence, nor for an unreviewed newer head mentioned by an older head's record. The one way a record can still be read for a head other than the one on what a human would call its own line is item 6.
6. Residual, bounded to a key line (should-fix 1, not blocking). Because the reader takes the FIRST line matching the key regex anywhere in the comment and tolerates blockquote, bullet and bold decoration, a `Head-sha:` line naming B that sits ABOVE the record's own line is the one the record names: probed as a blockquoted line, a bulleted bold line, a line inside a fenced code block, and a line placed before the `## Contract review` heading, each read as B (found at B, absent at A) at the PR head. This is not a regression (the base reader's whole-body scan read every one of them as B too), it needs a line-initial `Head-sha:` key line rather than prose, the template prints the line second so a template-shaped record is never affected, and the self-test's own ruling ('the FIRST line decides, a second one lower down is prose') is consistent with it. It is still a sha the author did not mean as the record's head, which the card's wanted item 1 says must never count, so it is recorded for a follow-up rather than waved through.

The guard's own fixture `recordComment` wrote `Head: ` on the first body line (the retired dialect) and now writes `Head-sha:`; the record-recognisers `RECORD` fixture moved the head from the heading tail to a `Head-sha:` line; the H51 battery's `DIALECT_A` / `DIALECT_B` fixtures stay as controls and gained `DIALECT_C` / `DIALECT_D`. Both PRs are merged, so no open PR reads differently. The corpus counts in the docblock (702 / 700 / 488) are the seat's own 123-page REST scan and were NOT re-measured here; the two named exceptions hold.

The second commit `40b5a25e2` only names the single legacy record precisely in that docblock; nothing else moves.

Rules face: none of the four files is a schema, an ADR or governed rules text (register and `reviewFace` agree), so no ④ is owed by face. Judged anyway because the card is p1 and the claim asked for the tier: the design is the right one. A record names one head on one key line, the accept set is one spelling (the one the template prints and 700 of 702 live records already use), the three legacy dialects are retired by count rather than bounded, and every reader reaches the head through a single exported function.
